# Aminoprofile

> Aminoprofile is a free web page for comparing the essential amino acids of foods. You search
> Aminoprofile's own open dataset of everyday foods by name (English, Dutch and other names), add
> foods to a table, set the amount of each in grams, and see the nine essential amino acids and
> protein per food and in total. The dataset (CC BY 4.0) is also published as files and through a
> read-only MCP server for AI agents.

- Values are in grams. The dataset gives them per 100 g of food. Aminoprofile scales them to the
  amount you set (100 g by default) and adds up the foods you tick.
- The amino acids are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine,
  threonine, tryptophan and valine. A missing value shows as a dash (—), which is not the same as 0.
  A total that includes a missing value is marked "≥".
- Under the total, a "Per g protein" row shows the mg of each essential amino acid in one gram
  of the ticked foods' protein, and a "Needed" row the mg the FAO (2013) scoring pattern for
  ages 3 and up asks (methionine with cystine, phenylalanine with tyrosine). Values under the
  bar are red, and the page then names foods with more of that amino acid. Not corrected for
  digestibility, so not a DIAAS.
- The search runs in the browser over the dataset, so nothing typed is sent anywhere. There is
  no account, no cookies and no stored history: the table lives in the browser tab. The page
  needs JavaScript and is made for desktop screens (1240 pixels wide or more).
- Agents: please use the MCP server or the dataset files below rather than scraping the pages.
- Aminoprofile is a non-commercial, open-source project by Damian Schilder: no ads, no
  accounts, no paid features. The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/damianschilder/aminoprofile)
  under the MIT licence.

## Pages

- [Search and compare](https://aminoprofile.com/): the search field, the results and the
  essential amino acids table.
- [Foods](https://aminoprofile.com/foods): the foods of the dataset by group, with protein,
  amino acid score and limiting amino acid. Each links to its own page, such as
  [Oats, rolled](https://aminoprofile.com/foods/oats-rolled): the amino acids per 100 g and per g
  protein, the score per amino acid, foods that complement it, how far the sources agree and the
  source entries.
- [Sources](https://aminoprofile.com/sources): every source the site rests on, numbered, with
  the licence of each database. Each (i) on the site links to its entries there.
- [Data](https://aminoprofile.com/data): the open dataset, how it is combined, its licence, and how to
  connect to the MCP server.
- [Privacy](https://aminoprofile.com/privacy): which data is involved (searches stay in the
  browser), who is responsible and what your rights are.

## Dataset

Aminoprofile foods, version 0.3.0 (November 2026, a draft). The essential amino acids, cystine,
tyrosine and protein of 206 everyday foods, in grams per 100 g edible portion, combined from four
national food composition databases. For every value it records which laboratories or databases
measured it, how many independent sources there are and how far they agree. Protein is
nitrogen x 6.25. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Credit Aminoprofile and the four sources.

- [aminoprofile-foods.json](https://aminoprofile.com/data/aminoprofile-foods.json): everything,
  with per value its origins, spread and flags, the links to the source entries and the source
  releases with SHA-256 hashes.
- [aminoprofile-foods.csv](https://aminoprofile.com/data/aminoprofile-foods.csv): the values and
  a quality summary per food, for spreadsheets.
- [Method, checks, known limits and credits](https://github.com/damianschilder/aminoprofile/blob/main/data/README.md)

## MCP server

- Endpoint: https://aminoprofile.com/mcp (MCP Streamable HTTP transport). Stateless, read-only,
  no login, CORS open. It answers from the dataset above.
- `search_foods` `{ query?, category?, limit? }`: foods with id, name, category, protein per
  100 g and the number of independent sources.
- `get_food` `{ id }`: grams per 100 g of protein and 11 amino acids, the food's amino acid score
  and limiting amino acid, the quality of the values (origins, independent sources, spread,
  estimated), links to the dataset and the method, and the licence.
- `score_foods` `{ items: [{ id, grams }] }`: totals in grams, the amino acid score of the
  combination per amino acid (FAO 2013 pattern for ages 3 and up, methionine with cystine,
  phenylalanine with tyrosine), the limiting amino acid and notes. Not corrected for
  digestibility, so not a DIAAS.
- Food ids look like `egg-whole-raw`, `peanut-butter` and `oats-rolled`.
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http aminoprofile https://aminoprofile.com/mcp`
- Claude (claude.ai and the desktop app): Settings, Connectors, add a custom connector with
  https://aminoprofile.com/mcp
- Other clients that support remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP: the same URL.

## Sources

The full list, with each database's prescribed credit, is on the
[Sources page](https://aminoprofile.com/sources).

The dataset, which the site's search and the MCP server answer from, combines four sources:

- [USDA FoodData Central](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/), SR Legacy (CC0). Citation: U.S.
  Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central: SR Legacy, 2018.
- [Bundeslebensmittelschlüssel (BLS) 4.0](https://doi.org/10.25826/Data20251217-134202-0), Max
  Rubner-Institut, Germany (CC BY 4.0).
- [Frida 5.5](https://doi.org/10.11583/DTU.29500682), the Danish Food Composition Database, DTU
  National Food Institute (CC BY 4.0).
- [Standard Tables of Food Composition in Japan, Amino Acids](https://www.mext.go.jp/), MEXT
  (Government of Japan Standard Terms of Use, compatible with CC BY 4.0).

The method and the scoring rest on:

- [FAO (2013)](https://openknowledge.fao.org/handle/20.500.14283/i3124e). Dietary protein
  quality evaluation in human nutrition. FAO Food and Nutrition Paper 92. The scoring pattern
  for older children, adolescents and adults is Table 5, p. 29. The score is the lowest ratio,
  p. 23.
- [Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2011/1169/oj), Annex I,
  point 10: protein = total Kjeldahl nitrogen x 6.25.
- [Moughan and Lim (2024)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnut.2024.1389719). Digestible indispensable
  amino acid score (DIAAS): 10 years on. Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1389719. Section 6.7: the
  score of a meal is calculated from the amino acids each food supplies.
- [FAO/INFOODS (2012)](https://www.fao.org/4/ap805e/ap805e.pdf). Guidelines for Food Matching,
  version 1.2.
- [Greenfield and Southgate (2003)](https://www.fao.org/4/y4705e/y4705e00.htm). Food composition
  data: production, management and use, second edition. FAO. Chapters 9 and 10.
